title: Compare two numbers
description:
Get two numbers from the user using input prompt. If a is greater than b return a is greater than b, if a is less b return a is smaller than b, else a is equal to b. Output:

```sh
Enter number one: 4
Enter number two: 3
4 is greater than 3
```

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `compare_numbers(a, b)`, returning the exact message `"{a} is greater than {b}"`, `"{a} is smaller than {b}"`, or `"{a} is equal to {b}"`.
examples:
compare_numbers(4, 3) -> '4 is greater than 3'
compare_numbers(3, 4) -> '3 is smaller than 4'
compare_numbers(3, 3) -> '3 is equal to 3'
hints: Use an if / elif / else chain to cover the three possible outcomes.
Compare a and b with > and < before falling back to the equal case.
Build each returned message with an f-string like f"{a} is greater than {b}".
expected_behavior: Returns a string comparing a and b: greater than, smaller than, or equal to, using the exact values passed in.
explanation: The three relational outcomes between two numbers - greater, smaller, or equal - are mutually exclusive, so an if / elif / else chain checks them in order and returns the matching formatted message.
